traits: Cap up to 10 cm, narrowly conical then umbonate and often lobed, yellow to orange or scarlet, viscid when young
Gills waxy, white to pale yellow or greyish
Stem up to 20 cm, fibrillose, yellow to orange-red, whitish at the base, no ring
Yellowish flesh; every part greys with age and finally turns black
Waxcap grassland, dunes, road verges · summer and autumn
safetyNote: Toxic: the DGfM lists it for a gastrointestinal syndrome. Wikipedia (en) says its edibility is unknown and that it may be poisonous, quoting Arora: reported poisonings may come from other species, and it may cause minor effects such as lightheadedness. There is no French Wikipedia page: the text comes from Wikipedia (en) and the DGfM. The most prudent status is kept.
